checks.lean:
example : T7.CoversBy T7.twoPointBasis := by
  intro b
  cases b
  · exact ⟨{false}, by simp [T7.twoPointBasis], rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨{true}, by simp [T7.twoPointBasis], rfl⟩
checks.message: The singleton basis must cover both Boolean points.

checks.lean:
example : T7.IntersectionRefines T7.twoPointBasis := by
  intro U hU V hV x hx
  simp [T7.twoPointBasis] at hU hV
  rcases hU with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hV with rfl | rfl <;> simp_all [T7.twoPointBasis]
checks.message: Whenever two basis singletons share a point, that same singleton must refine their intersection.

checks.lean:
example : T7.GeneratedOpen T7.twoPointBasis Set.univ := by
  refine ⟨T7.twoPointBasis, Set.Subset.rfl, ?_⟩
  ext b
  cases b <;> simp [T7.twoPointBasis]
checks.message: The basis generates `univ` as the union of its two singleton sets; it is not required to contain `univ`.

checks.lean: example : Set.univ ∉ T7.twoPointBasis := by simp [T7.twoPointBasis, Set.ext_iff]
checks.message: The singleton-only basis must not itself be a topology: added sets violate union closure.

checks.lean: example : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis (⋃ (a : ℚ) (b : ℚ) (_ : a < b), {Set.Ioo (a : ℝ) (b : ℝ)}) := Real.isTopologicalBasis_Ioo_rat
checks.message: Mathlib proves that open intervals with rational endpoints form a basis for the usual topology on ℝ.

hints.hint: Use `∀ x, ∃ U ∈ B, x ∈ U`.
Quantify `U,V` and `x ∈ U ∩ V`, then return `∃ W ∈ B, x ∈ W ∧ W ⊆ U ∩ V`.
Use `∃ C : Set (Set α), C ⊆ B ∧ s = ⋃₀ C`.
Use `{{true}, {false}}`; do not add `univ` to the basis itself.
